own_solution.law: Energy conservation with rolling without slipping: (1/2) m v^2 (1 + 2/5) = m g d sin(theta), so d = 0.7 v^2/(g sin theta) = 25.2/(9.8*0.42262) = 25.2/4.1417
assumptions: rolling without slipping (stated), static friction does no work
uniform solid sphere I = (2/5) m r^2

TD438.regime: pure rolling requires mu_s >= (2/7) tan(theta) = 0.133 at 25 degrees; 0.45 is above it

defect_reasons.other: The timing of the re-tilt in T96D5 ('is then tilted') and TDEF6 ('Before the sphere was set rolling... was tilted') is loosely worded; the intended reading (incline at 38 degrees during the climb) is the natural one but a mid-motion tilt or a since-reverted tilt are possible readings.

notes: R answer at 38 degrees: sin 38 = 0.61566, d = 25.2/(9.8*0.61566) = 25.2/6.0335 = 4.177 m; rolling still holds since (2/7) tan 38 = 0.223 < 0.45 (relevant only if friction is also given, which it is not in that sentence). Radius cancels (TACA4, T55FE same 8.5 cm). Earlier-experiment and solar-panel sentences are D. Variants consistent: 13 deg across TDEF6/T7B54/T96D5/T4182; 0.45 across friction pair; 8.5 cm across radius pair.
